verdicts.reason: A keeps the can inside its lavender circle, but the circle is cropped by the right edge, the logo is blown up to compete with the headline, and the NEW VIDEO badge is shrunk to a tag under the subcopy. B has the same logo and badge problems and also splits the can from its circle: the can sits alone on the left and an empty lavender disc floats on the right, so the circle becomes a meaningless blob.

A separates the product from its circle: an empty disc fills the left side and a bare can sits at the far right, and the logo is oversized. B keeps the can and circle together on the right (the circle is cropped at the edge), but it still has the oversized centered logo and the tiny, demoted NEW VIDEO badge.

A splits the can (left) from an empty circle (right), and its subcopy is shrunk to near-illegible fine print run inline with the badge. B keeps the can and circle composed together on the right with readable subcopy, though the circle is edge-cropped, the logo is oversized and the badge is tiny.

Both split the can from its circle, leaving an empty disc on the left and the can alone on the right, and both have an oversized logo. A also shrinks the subcopy to unreadable fine print beside the badge. B keeps the subcopy at a legible size, so its hierarchy is sounder even with the same broken imagery.
